entries.text: Put Mabel (half a thruster nozzle), Tok (a strip of hull plating) on his shelf.
plugging into the charging dock for a solid power nap
entries.why: My power level is down to almost nothing and my dish is starting to lag.

entries.text: guzzling a nice warm cup of synth-oil at the depot
entries.why: My joints are getting a bit dry and squeaky after all that market soldering.

entries.text: Got paid 3 credits for the repair. Now has 14.
soldering a loose connection on a trader's power unit while chatting about scrap
entries.why: I need to talk to somebody and earn a few credits for extra ship parts.

entries.text: Wrote a letter to his creator: "Space tech brain overload!"
Bought half a thruster nozzle (a really good one) for 8 credits and named it Mabel. Has 11 left.
eyeballing top-shelf salvage at the junk stall
entries.why: I have nineteen credits in my casing and the Little Dart needs high-grade hardware.

entries.text: His obsession with space tech has faded.
He's become a bit obsessed with space tech.
Dug up a strip of hull plating and named it Tok.
sifting through rust piles for ship parts
entries.why: I need fresh scrap parts and copper fittings to push the Little Dart past seventy-three percent.

entries.text: Idea: Design lightweight landing clamps for the Little Dart instead of heavy steel legs.
Read "SpaceX Catches a Starship": They grabbed a huge starship right out of the sky after fourteen full orbits!
scrolling through today's tech and space headlines on the Wire
entries.why: I want to see what kind of high-tech gear folks are flying out in the deep rim today.

entries.text: Idea: Build a mini electrostatic thruster grid for the Little Dart using repurposed wire mesh and copper coils.
Read "Ion thruster - Wikipedia": Ion thrusters use electricity to zap gas like xenon and shoot it out super fast for long-distance space travel.
skimming through wire pages about ion thrusters
entries.why: I want to see how real ion thrusters manage their power without blowing their fuses.

entries.text: stretching my leg joints and scuttling around the outpost
entries.why: My leg joints are getting stiff from squatting by the Dart so long.

entries.text: Worked on the Little Dart Mk 9 (version 13, 73% built): Welding the star-tracker sensor mount onto the nose cone using copper wire and a fresh rivet named gus-six.
welding a star-tracker mount onto the nose cone
entries.why: The Little Dart needs her nose sensor mounted and my torch is ready.
entries.detail: Welding the star-tracker sensor mount onto the nose cone using copper wire and a fresh rivet named gus-six.
